reason: Nobody disputes the 29 Sep half (no action). The claimed CHANGE to the post-deadline verdict does not hold up, for four reasons. (1) The count is off. The finding's matcher takes the nearest final node within 7 um for each daughter, not a one-to-one match. I re-ran the 9 cases with a Hungarian match over all GT and predicted nodes at t+1 (scratchpad r32b/merged_check.py -> merged_check_out.json). 6bba_afb141ff t48 has a second node at 6.15 um that the one-to-one match takes, and that node comes from another track, so the case is 'claimed', not merged. The class is 8/85 (9.4%), not 9 (11%). The ceiling is ~+0.006, not +0.007, and the 5 um floor still removes 2-3 of the 8. (2) This is a closed line in disguise. The 8 cases are a subset of R7-RC-B's MERGED class (31 of 668 missing GT nodes, 30 of them yx-dominant). R7 closed that class with 'only the detector or coordinate head can reach it = retraining, post-deadline'. The proposed trigger is 'at t+1 of a parent with only one child, add a 2nd daughter from sub-threshold map evidence 3-8 um from the child'. That is the v3 mirror/lowdet daughter (FINAL_REPORT l.410: ~0.5 TP vs ~1.5 FP public) with -LoG as the peak source. LoG changes where candidates come from. It does not change the precision problem that killed mirror/lowdet. (3) Precision is already measured against it. The forkblob lab on the exp60 control (CONTEXT 25 Sep 20:05Z) looked at one-blob forks with sister <= 5 um on x138: 150 forks gave evaluable TP 1, FP 6, ignored 143. One-blob forks are 24% of x138 forks but 2% of GT divisions. Break-even is FP:TP 2.8 (forkblob value verdict). A splitter that creates close sisters inside one blob fills that same population, so its expected evaluable FP:TP is ~6. The trigger population ('a surviving parent without a fork') is almost every non-leaf node in every frame, so it would fire far more often than the 8 true cases (~0.14 per clip). The only proposed discriminator, 'DaughterNet p', has not been measured on these 8 merged nodes: pairclass records DaughterNet p only for orphan candidates, and none exists here. (4) It cannot be tested. The lab has no heatmaps, so the 20% capture is the v3 toy, not data. The realistic ~1.6 TP (~+0.0012 lab gross) is then more than cancelled by ~6 FP per TP plus the node term (-0.0009 per +1% nodes). The in-sample lab detector also probably under-counts merges on unseen embryos, but it under-counts splitter FPs just as much. Net expected value ~0 to negative, public and private. It is not a new narrow line worth its own agenda slot.

Keep LoG-shoulders closed as dominated. If anyone reopens a post-hoc splitter, gate it first on a held-out measurement: the splitter's evaluable FP:TP must be <= 2 on exp60-style dumps with heatmaps, AND DaughterNet p on the 8 merged nodes must separate them from the forkblob one-blob FP forks. Change the curator line and the count 9 -> 8 in the round-32 report. No 29 Sep action, no build, no slot.
realistic_gain: 0 on 29 Sep (no build, not shippable after R8). Post-deadline, as a post-hoc splitter: ceiling ~+0.006 lab at perfect precision (8 TP). Realistic ~1.6 TP (~+0.0012 lab gross) minus ~6 evaluable FP per TP (forkblob composition, break-even 2.8) and node cost, so ~-0.001..+0.0003 lab. Public/private sign uncertain to negative. As a note under detector retraining it adds no score of its own.
